isid

Assert a compound key uniquely identifies rows

Stata 

isid g h

R tidystata 

tidystata::isid(data, g, h)

Assert a key is unique and nonmissing

Stata

joinby

Form every matching pair within groups

Stata 

joinby g using other.dta

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::inner_join(data,other,by='g',relationship='many-to-many')

Stata reference · R reference

Keep unmatched master rows while forming group pairs

Stata 

joinby g using other.dta, unmatched(master)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::left_join(data,other,by='g',relationship='many-to-many')

Differs from Stata Returns paired rows without the Stata _merge indicator.

merge

Record master-only, using-only and matched status

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using other.dta, generate(status)

R dplyr 

data$.master <- TRUE; other$.using <- TRUE; data <- dplyr::full_join(data,other,by='id',relationship='one-to-one'); data$status <- ifelse(is.na(data$.master),2L,ifelse(is.na(data$.using),1L,3L)); data$.master <- NULL; data$.using <- NULL

Requires disjoint non-key column names unless update is explicitly shown. dplyr suffixes overlapping names; ordinary Stata merge preserves master values, including master missing values, on matched rows.

Stata reference · R reference

7 more examples and alternatives

Keep all master rows in a one-to-one merge

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using other.dta, keep(master match) nogenerate

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::left_join(data,other,by='id',relationship='one-to-one')

Requires disjoint non-key column names unless update is explicitly shown. dplyr suffixes overlapping names; ordinary Stata merge preserves master values, including master missing values, on matched rows.

Stata reference · R reference

Stata reference · R reference

Perform a validated one-to-one full merge

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using other.dta, nogenerate

R dplyr 

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data$id),!anyDuplicated(other$id)); data <- dplyr::full_join(data,other,by='id',relationship='one-to-one')

Requires disjoint non-key column names unless update is explicitly shown. dplyr suffixes overlapping names; ordinary Stata merge preserves master values, including master missing values, on matched rows.

Stata reference · R reference

Fill master missing values from matched using values

Stata 

merge 1:1 id using other.dta, update nogenerate

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::full_join(data,other,by='id',suffix=c('','.using'),relationship='one-to-one'); data$x <- dplyr::coalesce(data$x,data$x.using); data$x.using <- NULL

Differs from Stata Shows value update only; Stata update conflict status codes 4/5 are not generated. Requires disjoint non-key column names unless update is explicitly shown. dplyr suffixes overlapping names; ordinary Stata merge preserves master values, including master missing values, on matched rows.

missings

Drop rows missing on every selected numeric variable

Stata 

missings dropobs x y, force

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::filter_out(data, dplyr::if_all(c(x, y), is.na))

filter_out() requires dplyr 1.2.0 or later.

Stata reference · R reference

Drop entirely missing numeric columns

Stata 

missings dropvars, force

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::select(data, !dplyr::where(~ all(is.na(.x))))

Differs from Stata Drops entirely missing columns of every type, not only numeric ones.

Stata reference · R reference

Report missing-value counts by numeric variable

Stata 

missings report x y

R tidystata 

tidystata::misstable(data, x, y)

Differs from Stata Lists variables with missing values, with counts and percentages.

Stata reference · R reference

Count numeric missing values within each row

Stata 

missings tag x y, generate(nmiss)

R tidystata 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, nmiss = tidystata::row_miss(x, y))

Stata reference · R reference

4 more examples and alternatives

Drop rows missing on every selected numeric variable

Stata 

missings dropobs x y, force

R base 

data <- data[rowSums(!is.na(data[c('x','y')]))>0,,drop=FALSE]

Stata reference · R reference

Drop entirely missing numeric columns

Stata 

missings dropvars, force

R base 

data <- data[!vapply(data,function(z) all(is.na(z)),logical(1))]

Differs from Stata Numeric-only fixture; Stata string missing is empty text and would require an additional R test for empty strings.

Stata reference · R reference

Report missing-value counts by numeric variable

Stata 

missings report x y

R base 

colSums(is.na(data[c('x','y')]))

Differs from Stata Numeric columns only. The R result includes zero counts; Stata report defaults to showing counts at least one.
